title: Zoom in: one product read, from local memory to the database
caption: Each check is cheaper than the next; only one request per key goes all the way to the database.

steps.text: Check the pod's own memory first: about 50 µs, but only the hottest products and only for 5 s.
Not there: one GET to the cache cluster, about 1 ms.
Hit: copy it into the local LRU for the next 5 s and return.

scenarios.name: Full miss
scenarios.summary: The first reader after an expiry pays for everyone: DB read, then SET with a jittered TTL.

steps.text: This request takes a short fill lock for the key (SET NX with a 2 s expiry).
Read the row from a replica.
SET it with 10 min plus up to 1 min of random jitter, so keys filled together don't expire together.

scenarios.name: Many misses at once
scenarios.summary: Hundreds of requests miss the same key in the same millisecond; only the lock winner reads the DB.

steps.text: 400 requests for a popular product all miss after its TTL ends.
One wins the fill lock and reads the DB.
The other 399 wait a few ms and read the cache again, which the winner has filled by then.

scenarios.name: Cache timeout
scenarios.summary: The cache cluster is slow or down: don't wait on it and don't let every request fall through to the DB.

steps.text: The GET times out after 20 ms.
Serve the local copy even if it is a few seconds past its TTL (stale beats down for a product page).
No local copy: read the DB, but only within a small per-pod limit of concurrent reads. Above it, return an error the page can render around.
